title: habitat flow
description: The YAML front matter of a flows/*.md file: how a core journey moves from screen to screen. The screens and transitions come from the Figma prototype's connections; the conditions, the unhappy paths and the rules come from the designer, because a prototype usually shows only the path where everything goes right.

status.description: 'draft' while it is being filled in, 'reviewed' once a person has checked it (no TODOs left), 'deprecated' when the journey no longer works this way.

owner.description: Who answers questions about this journey.

lastReviewed.description: When a person last checked this file against the prototype (YYYY-MM-DD).

name.description: The flow's name, e.g. 'Send an invoice'.

journey.description: The core journey in DESIGN.md this flow belongs to, in the same words.

page.description: The Figma page the prototype is on.

startingPoint.description: The name of the prototype's flow starting point.

nodeId.description: The node id of the first screen.

purpose.description: What the user is trying to get done, and what counts as done, in a sentence or two.

screens.description: The screens of the journey, in order, read from the prototype's top-level frames.

id.description: A short id that transitions refer to, e.g. 'review'.

name.description: The frame's name in Figma, or what the team calls the screen.

purpose.description: What this screen is for, in a sentence.

components.description: The design system components on the screen, by canonical name.

end.description: True when the journey is meant to finish here, so a screen with no way out is not reported as a dead end.

transitions.description: How the user moves between screens, read from the prototype's connections (Figma calls them reactions).

from.description: The id of the screen it starts on.

to.description: The id of the screen it leads to, or 'back' or 'close'.

trigger.description: What starts it, in Figma's words: click, hover, press, drag, key, after-delay, while-hovering, mouse-enter.

element.description: The layer that is clicked or pressed, e.g. 'Send invoice'.

component.description: The design system component the element is an instance of, e.g. 'Button'.

action.description: What happens: navigate to a screen, open an overlay (a dialog or sheet), swap an overlay, go back, close an overlay, scroll, open a link, or change a component's variant.

condition.description: When this transition is allowed or taken, e.g. 'only when every required field is valid'. Prototypes rarely show this; ask the designer.

unhappyPaths.description: What happens when things go wrong: errors, empty states, lost connections, cancelling halfway. A prototype rarely shows these, so they come from the designer.

then.description: What the user sees and can do next.

screen.description: The screen id it happens on.

antiPatterns.description: What an agent must never do in this journey, with the reason, as in a component file.

source.description: Who stated this rule and when.

evidence.description: Research insights the flow as a whole rests on.
